pr_comments:
This fixes a important mutex error:
When ONVIF long polling is used, the long polling request would hold the send_mutex lock for up to 5 minutes.
All other requests and communications to the camera were blocked untill the long_polling request would finish.

Did not notice this during earlier testing because my camera returns the long_polling request every 20 seconds, so the requests were only delayed by a maximum of 20 seconds (still very bad).
On some cameras like the older E1 this can be 60 seconds (a lot worse).

This mutex problem has been resolved in the upstream library with version 0.7.6

@Efekent thank you for the detailed explanation of the problem.
This issue consists of 2 parts:
1) The timeout and subsequent connection errors occuring.
2) The reolink integration failing to properly recover and receiving visitor events again.

About part 1: this is probably caused by one of the following:
- a issue in your network, like the router dropping the connection
- too many open (ONVIF) connections to the camera, causing the camera to drop connections (do other programms like blue iris or simular also acces the doorbell?)
- a firmware bug in the doorbell camera (I know some users are running beta firmware from reolink support that apperently improves these issues. Personnaly I have not experianced issues with my 2 doorbells, but those are connected through a NVR).

Basically there is not much I can do about part 1, your best bet is to contact reolink support and see if they can help you (with beta firmware), clearly explain the problem and please note you are using it with HomeAssistant.

About part 2: This is something I schould be able to fix in the code.
My susspision is that some exception occurs in the ONVIF long polling loop, causing that task to exit and not recover.
Although I could not find a abvious place where this could happen.
To confirm this, could you disable the automation that restarts the reolink integration, then enable debug logging of the reolink integration of the doorbell giving issues. Then restart the integration and let it run in debug mode untill the problem occurs. Please confirm you are not receiving visitor events while debug is still on, then let it run for another 15 minutes in debug logging (to see how it attempts recoveries). Then stop debug logging and post the .txt debug log here.

Do note the ONVIF pushes will not work due to the SSL certificate, therefore the integration will fall back on ONVIF long polling which has a slightly higher latency and is more demanding on the camera (more HTTP(S) communication with the camera required). ONVIF long polling schould receive events with <0.5s lattency while ONVIF push achieves <0.1s lattency in my tests.
See the new docs about this: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/reolink/#reducing-latency-of-motion-events

@Efekent After a full day of unplugging and plugging in the network cable of my test camera I figured it out :)
I was able to create connection errors in this way and observe how the integration recoverd, and spotted some strange behaviour.
Eventually I figured out what was going on:

When using ONVIF long polling, the long poll request would obtain a shared mutex lock, blocking all communication to the camera from other requests for up to 60 seconds. This includes the requests needed to re-subscribe to the ONVIF long polling. Therefore this not only made the integration extremly slow when using ONVIF long polling, it could also lead to nasty situations in which the integration was not able to recover fast from temporary network errors.

I fixed these issues (together with some additionally found bugs) in the upstream reolink_aio library and released version 0.7.6.
This PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/97464 will make HA use that new version.

Additionally I found another problem: once the network was lost, the old long_polling request would first need to timeout which takes 5 minutes. I fixed that in this PR: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/97465, such that upon re-subscription to the ONVIF long polling, the old long_polling request is emidiatly canceled and a new one is started such that we can start receiving events again as soon as we resubscribe.

Once those 2 PRs are merged, there is a good change that your problems go away.
I will let you know when they are incorporated in a new HA (beta) release such that you can test them.

If you appreciate the reolink integration and want to support its development, please consider [sponsering](https://github.com/sponsors/starkillerOG) the upstream library or purchase Reolink products through [this affiliate link](https://reolink.pxf.io/q44QWq).

review_comments:
Inside the reolink_aio library the request is tried `RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (=3) with a timeout of `host.api.timeout`, if it then fails it will disconnect from the camera, invalidade the tokens and unsubscribe from the ONVIF connections. This unsubscribing needs two additional requests that are tried only once with a host.api.timeout, so that is the +2.

Furthermore the timeouts schould be handeled properly in the upstream library so this `async_timeout.timeout` inside HA schould never be reached. However in the past a few times complex unexpected issues have resulted in mutex problems that can hang the request for multiple minutes. This `async_timeout.timeout` is a falesafe for those kind of unexpected issues, (that have all been solved by now by my knoladge, but of course there can always be unknown bugs).
